title: cross-region-bid-sensitivity-and-heuristics-wip
content:
Context / intent:
- Quick working spreadsheet and heuristic notes for cross-region spot/on-demand bidding strategies and fallback tiers.
- Goal: produce a simple decision rule set + sensitivity matrix we can hand to routing + pricing teams and to the simulation infra.
- This is intentionally lightweight — metrics + Monte Carlo sims to follow (RD-1423).

Assumptions (baseline):
- Serving model: mix of gpt-small-ish open models that fit well on 2xA10G equiv. (we parameterize per GPU).
- Traffic: 2M tokens/day baseline for test fleet (scale up later).
- SLOs: P50 latency <= 60ms, P95 <= 180ms. Premium customers have P95 <= 120ms.
- Retry penalty: cold-fallback retry to on-demand adds average latency +40ms and ~0.2 extra tokens per request (prompt re-send overhead).
- Spot preemption behavior: modeled as Poisson with mean preemption rate p (varies by region).

Baseline cost table (sample inputs for the model):
| region    | on_demand_usd_hr | spot_usd_hr | est_preempt_pct_day | gpu_qps | typical_seq_len | comments |
|-----------|------------------:|-----------:|--------------------:|--------:|----------------:|---------|
| us-east-1 | 3.60              | 1.05       | 8%                  | 200     | 64              | large capacity, low latency
| us-west-2 | 3.80              | 1.20       | 12%                 | 180     | 64              | slightly higher spot churn
| eu-west-1 | 3.90              | 1.30       | 10%                 | 170     | 64              | higher egress to NA
| ap-southeast-1 | 3.20         | 0.96       | 20%                 | 160     | 64              | cheaper on-demand, high spot churn

Quick formula sketch (sheet-friendly):
- compute_cost_per_hour = active_gpus * price_per_gpu_hr
- tokens_served_per_hour = qps * seq_len * 3600
- base_cost_per_1M_tokens = (compute_cost_per_hour / tokens_served_per_hour) * 1_000_000
- effective_cost_with_preempt = base_cost + (preempt_rate * fallback_cost_per_preempt)
- fallback_cost_per_preempt approximated as: (time_loss_penalty * token_rate * token_price_equivalent) + on_demand_additional_compute

Sample computed numbers (rounded):
- us-east-1 on-demand base_cost_per_1M_tokens = 3.60 / (200*64*3600) * 1e6 ≈ $0.78 per 1M tokens (note: unrealistically small here, but placeholders for per-shape tuning).
- us-east-1 spot base_cost_per_1M_tokens = 1.05 / (...) ≈ $0.23 per 1M tokens
- With 8% preempt and fallback overhead (estimated $0.15 per preempt event), effective spot cost ~ $0.23 + 0.08*0.15 ≈ $0.242

Sensitivity matrix (example rows):
- Varied inputs: [spot_price_pct_of_on_demand, preempt_rate, cross_region_egress_usd_per_1M_tokens, additional_latency_ms_on_fallback] 
- Output: recommended routing choice (prefer spot / prefer on-demand / mixed with X% hedging), expected_cost_delta, impact_on_SLOs.

Matrix sample (compact):
| scenario | spot_pct | preempt% | egress$/1M | latency_penalty_ms | recommended | cost_delta_vs_all-on-demand | SLO_risk | notes |
|---------:|---------:|---------:|-----------:|-------------------:|------------|----------------------------:|--------:|------|
| A        | 30%      | 5%       | 0.05       | 20                 | spot-first | -22%                       | low     | local region, low churn
| B        | 32%      | 15%      | 0.12       | 50                 | mixed (70/30) | -8%                    | med     | consider cache tier 1
| C        | 25%      | 25%      | 0.25       | 80                 | on-demand prefer | +2% (spot worse)    | high    | high preempt + egress cost

Heuristics / routing rules (working):
1) Traffic tiering first: classify traffic into {premium, latency-sensitive, best-effort}.
2) For premium: prefer reserved/dedicated -> on-demand fallback only. No spot. (SLOs matter).
3) For latency-sensitive non-premium: prefer regional on-demand; allow spot in-region only if preempt_rate < 10% and spot price < 40% of on-demand. If preempt triggers, fallback to same-region on-demand.
4) For best-effort / background jobs: prefer spot across cheap regions, allow cross-region routing. Hedge by reserving X% capacity in target region to reduce retry spikes.
5) Cross-region decision rule: route to remote region if expected_cost_savings_per_request > latency_cost_threshold and preempt-adjusted_savings > 0. In practice: require >15% adjusted savings and expected added P95 < 40ms.
6) Fallback tiers (fast path):
   - tier0: same-region on-demand (fastest, default fallback)
   - tier1: same-region degraded model (quantized variant) — cheaper CPU or smaller GPU footprint; if accuracy acceptable for request type
   - tier2: cross-region on-demand
   - tier3: queued/retry with cached response (best for idempotent or cached-able prompts)

Bid strategy heuristics (spot):
- Use adaptive bid floors per region: target 35–45% of on-demand for steady-state, adjust upward when predicted queue/backlog > 30% to reduce preempt risk.
- Increase bid by +10–20% for regions serving latency-sensitive tiers even if traffic labeled non-premium, to reduce false-positive preempts.
- Use short TTLs for spot reservations for burst/elastic workloads; longer reservations for background pipelines.

Monte Carlo notes (next steps):
- Simulate 30 days with per-region preempt_time_distribution from historical spot traces (RD-1802).
- Metrics to capture: cost per 1M tokens, P50/P95 latency distribution, percent of requests rerouted cross-region, preempt_count, percent of requests hitting fallback quantized model.
- Run sim with 3 policy families: 
   P1 (conservative): spot only for best-effort, 0% spot for premium/latency-sensitive.
   P2 (balanced): allow spot for latency-sensitive if preempt<10% and spot<45% price; hedging 20% reserved capacity.
   P3 (aggressive): spot-first for non-premium; use cross-region aggressively when price delta>20%.

Quick spreadsheet checklist (for the sim owner):
- [ ] Pull regional spot history CSV (last 90 days) — source: infra/spot-tracker
- [ ] Normalize prices to per-GPU baseline (A10G equiv) — PR #58 has conversion map
- [ ] Add egress cost buckets by region pairs
- [ ] Implement retry/fallback latency model (simple additive ms + probability)

Open questions / trade-offs to discuss in sync with routing infra (Xinyi):
- How do we safely expose cross-region routing to customers? opt-in vs opt-out? implications for data residency.
- Should we model SLO penalties as dollarized (blended SLA credits) or as hard constraint? Product prefers SLA-dollarization for pricing math but infra wants hard limits.
- Where to store per-customer routing policy (console + API) so rollouts can be per-customer? minimal viable UX: toggle with buckets.

Action items (short):
- Maya: spin up initial Monte Carlo run w/ P1/P2/P3 by 2026-03-05 (RD-1423).
- Liam: attach spot history and conversion table to the sheet (github/pull/58) — due 2026-02-20 (blocking).
- Xinyi: validate latency models against production p95 traces (serving-runtime team).
- Priya: draft console UX copy for "cross-region cost-optimized routing" (customer-facing note).

Notes / low-fi commentary (scratch):
- Early experiments show cross-region can save 18–35% on compute but add 0–60ms depending on pair and egress. For many background and cached flows this is a clear win.
- We should add a "degraded-model" column in the cost model: when we send to quantized model we get ~30% cost reduction and ~5–10% drop in output quality (task-dependent).

References and helpful links: RD-1423 (routing sim), RD-1802 (historical spot), github.com/redwood/optimizer/pull/58, confluence.redwood.com/display/OPT/Cross-Region+Routing+Notes

End of working sheet notes — comments inline welcome.
